notes:
### Changed
- **Progressive first launch:** seeding now writes English first and makes the
  app usable immediately; Japanese and Chinese finish in the background with a
  small non-blocking status line. Previously all three catalogues (~70k cards)
  blocked the splash screen before first paint.
- **Incremental seeding:** each language is written as an idempotent upsert and
  only its own rows are reconciled afterwards, replacing the clear-and-rebuild
  that emptied the library while it ran. An interrupted language resumes on the
  next launch, and installs upgrading from the previous release adopt their
  existing data instead of rewriting ~70k rows.
- **Search:** prepared keys are built once and reused, and a broad query now
  keeps only the first page in order instead of sorting every match. Worst-case
  query drops from ~17 ms to ~2 ms with identical ordering; searches are also
  now punctuation- and accent-insensitive ("mrmime" finds "Mr. Mime").
- **Card grid:** long sets are windowed. A 782-card set renders ~44 tiles and
  keeps its full scroll height, instead of mounting all 782.
- **PWA:** the English catalogue is precached, so a first launch installed while
  offline can seed. Japanese/Chinese chunks stay runtime-cached.
- **Scan-index memory:** fingerprints keep the illustration grid in the packed
  int8 form the published shards already use (plus a per-record NCC scale)
  instead of inflating it into a JS number array. The retained index measures
  5,074 → 1,425 bytes/card, about **336 MB → 94 MB** for the 69,439-record
  canonical index. Ranking is numerically unchanged (worst per-reference score
  delta 4.4e-16; a real reference card still self-matches at 1.0000), and the
  on-device fingerprint path now writes the same shape.
- **Data migration:** Dexie v14 clears the derived fingerprints and their
  `scanIndexSha:*` markers so the next launch re-downloads them. Collection,
  wishlist, prices, grades and saved scans are untouched.
- **Graded comps:** PkmnPrices eBay sold comps are now the only source
  (card-scoped by set + number, exact attribution, `lookbackDays` window).
  Removed the eBay/SoldComps integrations and all their settings (eBay Client
  ID/Secret, marketplace, sandbox, SoldComps key/budget), plus active eBay
  listings and the "Prefer realized eBay sales" setting — asking prices are not
  evidence of value, and the extra setup only served power users. PriceCharting
  remains a reference.

### Fixed
- **PkmnPrices October 2026 API changes:** lookups now send the language
  explicitly (English/Japanese) and ask the detail endpoint for USD, so names
  without the old trailing number and the new language gating behave correctly.
  A plan-gated `403` (for example Japanese on a Free key) is reported as a plan
  restriction instead of a rejected key, and a `429` uses the API's
  `error.limit_type`, `Retry-After`, `retry_after`/`resets_at` and
  `upgrade_url` to say which limit was hit and when it clears (per-minute vs
  the daily credit allowance) rather than guessing.
- **PkmnPrices proxy quota headers:** the Worker now forwards and exposes
  `x-credits-*`, `x-rate-*`, `Retry-After` and `Warning`, and never replays
  credit/rate headers from its edge cache (a cache hit costs no credit).
  Settings → PkmnPrices **Test** works without a personal key, bypasses the
  cache, and shows live credits/requests plus any API warning.
- **Japanese PkmnPrices fallback:** the set map only carried pre-migration ids,
  so canonical `ja-pkmndb-*` cards never reached PkmnPrices. Added 338
  name-matched Japanese set ids (plus the legacy aliases), restoring Japanese
  price lookups (verified against Expansion Pack Pikachu).
- **Set/number matching:** card resolution now prefers an exact set name over
  prefix containment, so "Base Set" cannot match "Base Set 2", and collector
  numbers are compared with leading zeros/`No.` normalized. This prevents a
  price or comp from the wrong set/printing.

No descriptor change (`SCAN_VERSION` stays 5) and no PKMNDB change: the
published `scan/canonical` index is unaffected.
